_comment: Drives the study roadmap page (site/build-roadmap.js -> _site/data/roadmap.json, rendered by site/pages/lc-roadmap.html). Each node is one topic in the dependency graph: `prereqs` are the topics you should have done first (these become the drawn edges), `row` is the layer it sits on (must be greater than every prereq's row — the build enforces it), `sheets` are doc/cheatsheet slugs, and `problems` are LeetCode ids that must exist in README.md's tables. Titles, difficulty and repo solution links are resolved from README.md at build time, so they are never duplicated here.

meta.title: Study Roadmap
meta.intro: A dependency graph over the topics in this repo. Start at the top, unlock a topic once its prerequisites are done, and tick problems off as you solve them — progress is stored in your browser.

_lists_comment: The problem sets the page's dropdown offers. `from` says where membership comes from: `curated` = the ids on the nodes below; `list:<flag>` = a flag in data/problem_lists.json (refresh with script/fetch_problem_lists.py); `readme:<field>` = a marker in README.md's own tables. `topicFrom` names the taxonomies, in order, that decide which topic each problem lands in — the first one that maps wins, so a coarse source can fall through to a finer one.

lists.label: Roadmap picks
lists.blurb: The curated path — a handful of problems per topic, in teaching order.

lists.label: Blind 75
lists.blurb: The original Blind list: 75 problems chosen for coverage, not volume.

lists.label: NeetCode 150
lists.blurb: Blind 75 widened to 150 — the usual full-coverage target.

lists.label: NeetCode 250
lists.blurb: NeetCode 150 plus 100 more, for a second pass on the weaker patterns.

lists.label: NeetCode (all)
lists.blurb: Everything NeetCode has filed under a pattern. Far more than an interview loop needs.

lists.label: Google-tagged
lists.blurb: Every problem this repo's README tags `google`.

lists.label: MUST
lists.blurb: The repo's own must-know marker — the same set as doc/must_lc_list.md.

_topicSources_comment: Each source files problems under its own taxonomy; these maps put them on roadmap topics. `null` means "deliberately not on the roadmap" (SQL, shell, JavaScript-only exercises). The build fails on a key that is missing, points at an unknown topic, or is mapped but unused — so a new upstream category cannot silently drop a whole group of problems.

nodes.title: Arrays & Hashing
nodes.blurb: The root of everything: index arithmetic, and trading space for O(1) lookup.

nodes.title: Two Pointers
nodes.blurb: Converging, trailing and fast/slow pointers — the cheapest way to drop a nested loop.

nodes.title: Stack
nodes.blurb: LIFO discipline: matching, nesting and expression evaluation.

nodes.title: Prefix Sum
nodes.blurb: Precompute once, answer any range in O(1). Pair it with a hash map for subarray counting.

nodes.title: Bit Manipulation
nodes.blurb: XOR tricks, masks and the lowest set bit. Small topic, occasionally decisive.

nodes.title: Math & Number Theory
nodes.blurb: Digit handling, overflow, primes and modular arithmetic.

nodes.title: Sliding Window
nodes.blurb: Expand on a condition, contract when it breaks. A whole question family with one template.

nodes.title: Binary Search
nodes.blurb: Halving a monotonic space. Get the boundary templates exact and the variants fall out.

nodes.title: Linked List
nodes.blurb: Pointer surgery. Low conceptual depth, high implementation-precision bar.

nodes.title: Monotonic Stack
nodes.blurb: "Next greater / previous smaller" in one pass, by keeping the stack sorted.

nodes.title: Matrix / 2D Grid
nodes.blurb: Row/column indexing, in-place rotation, and 2D range sums.

nodes.title: String Algorithms
nodes.blurb: Substring search beyond the naive scan: KMP, rolling hash, and expand-around-centre.

nodes.title: Trees & BST
nodes.blurb: How DFS state flows down and back up. The single largest interview surface after arrays.

nodes.title: Sorting & Selection
nodes.blurb: What sorting buys you, custom comparators, and quickselect for top-k without a heap.

nodes.title: Binary Search on the Answer
nodes.blurb: Guess the answer, write a monotone feasibility check, binary search on it. The most under-practised tier-5 skill.

nodes.title: Heap & Priority Queue
nodes.blurb: "Repeatedly take the best" and top-k. Two heaps give you a running median.

nodes.title: Trie
nodes.blurb: Prefix trees: shared-prefix lookup, wildcard matching, and word-search pruning.

nodes.title: Backtracking
nodes.blurb: Choose, recurse, un-choose. Subsets, permutations, and the pruning that makes them tractable.

nodes.title: Graphs (BFS / DFS)
nodes.blurb: Traversal and connectivity on grids and adjacency lists. BFS on an unweighted graph is shortest path.

nodes.title: Greedy
nodes.blurb: Sort, then take the locally best choice — and be ready to justify it with an exchange argument.

nodes.title: Design a X
nodes.blurb: Compose the structures you already know to hit a per-operation complexity target.

nodes.title: 1-D Dynamic Programming
nodes.blurb: Start from the recursion you wrote for backtracking, memoise it, then flatten to a table.

nodes.title: Union Find
nodes.blurb: Disjoint sets with path compression — connectivity under incremental merges.

nodes.title: Topological Sort
nodes.blurb: Kahn's in-degree peeling on a DAG. Also how you detect a cycle in a dependency graph.

nodes.title: Intervals & Sweep Line
nodes.blurb: Sort by start or end, then sweep. Get the overlap predicate right once and reuse it.

nodes.title: Segment Tree & Fenwick
nodes.blurb: Reach for these only when you need range queries *and* point updates — otherwise a prefix sum is enough.

nodes.title: 2-D Dynamic Programming
nodes.blurb: Two indices, one table. Grid paths, two-string alignment, and interval DP.

nodes.title: Knapsack DP
nodes.blurb: 0/1 vs unbounded, and the loop order that separates them. Recognise it and the rest is mechanical.

nodes.title: Advanced Graphs
nodes.blurb: Weighted shortest paths, MST and Eulerian paths. Mostly L5+ territory — know which algorithm fits.
